resources.string: Moli could not start. Your data is preserved.
Test build. Encrypted backup is available while stopped. Restore requires a fresh installation; keep the file and password separately. Do not use irreplaceable data yet.
4 to 32 digits — keep this code safe
The Moli server is running on this tablet.
The protected key cannot be opened. A new key will not be generated.

Stop Moli before backup. The encrypted file includes data, configuration, vault key and dashboard code. Choose a long unique password and keep it separately: recovery requires it. Restore never replaces a configured installation and does not start the server. Limit: 512 MiB, 10,000 internal files. External files referenced by paths are not included. Future Linux compatibility has not been tested. This test app is independent of the earlier prototype and cannot automatically access its data.
Stop the server and wait for shutdown to finish before continuing.
Restore refused: this installation already has a key. Use a fresh test installation; do not uninstall your prototype for this test.
Use at least 16 characters, preferably several random words. This password also protects the vault key. A lost password cannot be recovered.
16 to 1,024 characters; both entries must match.
Backup / restore in progress… Keep this window open.
Operation complete. Keep the file and password separately. After restore, start Moli manually.
Operation refused or interrupted: check the password, file, free space and compatibility. No active data was replaced. An interrupted export must be recreated.

Before updating: stop Moli, export an encrypted backup and keep its password separately. Install the new APK over this app, then reopen Moli and start the server. Android preserves data when the package name and signature remain compatible and the version increases. If Android refuses, do not uninstall or clear data. Demo APKs guarantee signing continuity only within one delivery. Moving to a future durable release will use restoration into a new installation.

Notifications: %1$s
Android battery: %2$s
These states do not prove extended sleep reliability. Samsung may apply additional restrictions. After reboot or force-stop, reopen Moli manually.

%1$s
Last success: %2$s s
Successes / failures this session: %3$d / %4$d
Longest interval without a check: %5$d s
Successful starts in this installation: %6$d

Each success comes from an authenticated local HTTP request to the Rust engine. A notification alone proves nothing. Checks run every 30 s when Android allows it. A long gap can indicate suspension; success after waking does not prove continuous operation during sleep. Record counters before and after. No forced wake or battery changes.

Initialize Moli with a test PIN, then stop the engine before changing integrations. Imports are limited to the internal synthetic source and Open-Meteo HTTPS: no physical devices, secrets or writes. Start the engine to see values here and in the dashboard.
Synthetic devices from the native Demo driver. No network connection. Approve activation?

Read-only HTTPS to api.open-meteo.com, public Paris test coordinates 48.8566 / 2.3522, no key. Updated forecast data, not a measurement at your home. Requests and your IP are visible to the provider. Approve?
Read-only HTTP to a synthetic source owned by this app. No local network device. Simulated values: 42.5 °C and 55%.

File review (the profile name may contain a synthetic value):
File: %1$s
Profile: %2$s
SHA-256 of reviewed bytes: %3$s
%4$s
Points: %5$d
GET requests (path and interval in seconds): %6$s
Selection saved. Press Start to activate. Settings persist; no previous data deleted.
Initialize the PIN on the main screen before configuring integrations.
Stop the engine and wait until it has stopped before changing integrations.
Changed profile or invalid approval: activation refused. Stop, reimport and review the file, or restore the previous selection.

Import refused: valid read-only UTF-8 TOML, at most 64 KiB. Only the hostless /status example and supplied Open-Meteo profile are accepted: no secrets, custom headers, writes or other destinations. Also check initialization and available storage.
Engine stopped: no current data verified.
Data unavailable: initialize or start the engine and retry. Old values do not prove connectivity.
Integration selected; waiting for data. Fresh values cannot be guaranteed during a network failure.
Press Back again to close the interface.
Press Back again to close the interface. The server stays active.
No recent check: monitor not scheduled or still pending
Last executed check: engine did not respond correctly
A large gap means no check, not a proven HTTP failure. Failures count actual attempted requests. The start counter identifies a new engine instance, not simply reopening the UI.
Last successful engine read: %1$s (%2$d reads). Display refreshed every 5 seconds while this page remains open.
No confirmed engine read for this check. Start the engine or try again.
Open-Meteo: new weather request every 15 minutes. Reading the display does not force an Internet request; values may remain unchanged.
Trial journal recording: %1$d events. Export only when you request it.
Journal stopped: %1$d events. Starting a trial replaces only the previous journal.
One-time weather check: not performed yet. Its result will appear here, separately from engine values.
One-time HTTPS check in progress, up to about 12 seconds…
Real HTTPS check succeeded: %1$.1f °C, humidity %2$.0f %%, received %3$s. Location approved in settings. One-time result, separate from the engine stream (15 min).
Check not started: wait at least one minute between attempts; at most ten per hour. Normal weather polling continues.
Add and approve Open-Meteo with the engine stopped before this check. No request was sent.
No valid check result: verify Internet and approval. No new weather data confirmed; normal engine operation is unchanged.
Journal saved to the selected file. No automatic transmission.
Export not completed. Verify the destination and try again; no automatic transmission.

GUIDED TRIAL — states below are observed evidence, not automatic validation.
1. Start a trial, then Stop before changing integrations. Expected: engine stopped. Observed: %1$s.
2. Choose synthetic-temperature.toml (or Synthetic example), review and Approve. Expected: saved profile. Observed: %2$s.
3. Optionally add Demo, then Start. Expected: 42.5 °C received with a timestamp under Values. Observed: synthetic read %3$s; Demo %4$s.
4. Stop, Add Open-Meteo and approve. Expected: weather saved. Observed: %5$s. Check weather now for an immediate HTTPS result here; Start for the normal stream under Values. Engine observation: %6$s.
5. End trial, then Export text journal to keep it or voluntarily share the results.
Stop the engine, edit settings, then Save and Start. Tablet readings stay local; no GPS.
Saving allows these coordinates to be sent to Open-Meteo via HTTPS every 15 minutes. No account needed. Public example: Paris, 48.8566 / 2.3522. The name stays local.
Prepare rooms here. Use existing Moli functions to assign equipment after adding a compatible integration. No real device is added or controlled.
Settings saved. Start the engine and return to the dashboard.
Check name and coordinates; up to 32 rooms, 60 characters each.
Settings may be incomplete: check them before starting and retry.
